title: Equivalence arrows are initial in the fixed-source twisted-arrow simplicial set
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, equivalence edges, initial objects and mapping spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and the ordered join from [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a quasicategory and $x\in\mathcal C_0$. For $n\geq0$, let $(P_x)_n$ consist of maps $N([n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n])\to\mathcal C$ whose restriction to the first ordered block is the constant map at $x$. The operator for $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ is precomposition with $N(\theta^{\mathrm{op}}\star\theta)$. Assume that the resulting simplicial set $P_x$ is a quasicategory. Every equivalence edge $f:x\to y$ of $\mathcal C$, viewed as a vertex of $P_x$, is initial: for every vertex $g$ of $P_x$, $\operatorname{Map}_{P_x}(f,g)$ is weakly contractible. In particular the degenerate identity edge at $x$ is initial in $P_x$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.1: initiality of an equivalence arrow in the fixed-source twisted-arrow category. Only the initiality conclusion is used; the quasicategory property of P_x is assumed separately here to keep this auxiliary statement independent of its parent left-fibration theorem. Kerodon tag 03JW, not a Stacks tag. Online statement and full proof read; archival source WANTED.

proof.text: For the unique map $p:P_x\to\Delta^0$, the inner-fibration lifting condition is exactly the inner-horn filling condition of the assumed quasicategory $P_x$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary]. Its $p$-initiality condition is precisely initiality in this item: the mapping simplicial set between the unique vertex of $\Delta^0$ and itself has exactly one simplex in each degree, so a mapping-space map to it is a weak homotopy equivalence exactly when its source is weakly contractible, as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Thus it suffices, for every $n>0$, to extend each $a:\partial\Delta^n\to P_x$ with $a(0)=f$ to $\Delta^n\to P_x$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.1, boundary-filling reduction (there cited as Proposition 4.7.3.11); the existing dependency states this criterion in the relative form of Corollary 7.1.5.17 (Kerodon 02WS), specialized here to the map to a point.

proof.text: Use $V_n$ and the basic-face union $K_0$ of [lem-coef-infinity-twisted-pullback-boundary-filtration]. Number the vertices of $[n]^{\mathrm{op}}\star[n]$ by $0,\ldots,2n+1$: the first copy of $j\in[n]$ has position $n-j$ and the second has position $n+1+j$. Its nerve is therefore $\Delta^{2n+1}$, by the nerve and join formulas in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [lem-coef-infinity-pushout-join-saturation]. The face of $\partial\Delta^n$ omitting $j$ gives a map on the face omitting the pair $\{n-j,n+1+j\}$. These are exactly the maximal faces of basic type (b). The fixed-source requirement gives the constant map at $x$ on the face $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, of basic type (a). All these maps agree on intersections: intersections of boundary faces are their common simplicial restrictions, and intersections with the first block are constant at $x$. Degreewise gluing thus gives $\theta_0:K_0\to\mathcal C$. Its edge $\{n,n+1\}$ is $f$, since it corresponds to the vertex $0$ of the boundary. This edge belongs to $K_0$ even when $n=1$, since it omits the pair $\{0,2n+1\}$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.1, basic subsets and identification of the boundary data with a map on K_0.

proof.text: Take the list $S_1,\ldots,S_m$ and unions $K_q$ provided by [lem-coef-infinity-twisted-pullback-boundary-filtration]. The map is already defined on $K_0$. At stage $q$ set $i=\operatorname{pr}(S_q)$ and write $S_q=\{j_0<\cdots<j_d\}$ with $i=j_k$. The cited intersection equality says that the restriction of the existing map to the new face is prescribed exactly on $\Lambda_k^d$. Hence a filler for this horn extends the map to $K_q$: in each simplicial degree glue the two functions on $K_{q-1}$ and $\Delta^{S_q}$ along their equal restrictions. The resulting functions commute with restriction operators because each of the two functions does. This supplies the gluing directly, with no separate pushout theorem.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.1, priority ordering, horn intersection and union extension.

proof.text: The definition in [lem-coef-infinity-twisted-pullback-boundary-filtration] implies that a nonbasic $S_q$ meets each of the $n+1$ disjoint pairs, and prioritized means that it contains both $i$ and $2n+1-i$ in one of these pairs. Thus $|S_q|\geq n+2$ and $d\geq2$. Also $2n+1-i>i$ belongs to $S_q$, so $k<d$. If $0<k<d$, fill the horn using the quasicategory condition of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. If $k=0$ and $i<n$, maximality of $i$ implies $2n-i\notin S_q$. Since the pair $\{i+1,2n-i\}$ must be met, $i+1\in S_q$; these are the first two vertices. Their edge lies in the first block, so its image under the already constructed map is the degenerate identity at $x$. It is an equivalence, witnessed by the constant two-simplices. If $k=0$ and $i=n$, the first two vertices are $n,n+1$, and the edge is the prescribed equivalence $f$. In each $k=0$ case apply [lem-cbc-equivalence-outer-horn-filling], whose dimension requirement $d\geq2$ has just been checked. All possibilities have now been covered, and Step 3 glues each filler to an extension on $K_q$.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.1, inner-horn case, exclusion of the final horn, and the two initial-horn cases.

proof.text: Induct over $q=1,\ldots,m$, keeping the restriction to every previous union fixed. By [lem-coef-infinity-twisted-pullback-boundary-filtration], $K_m=\Delta^{2n+1}$, so this produces $\theta:\Delta^{2n+1}\to\mathcal C$ extending $\theta_0$. Its first block is still constant at $x$, being contained in $K_0$. It therefore defines an $n$-simplex of $P_x$, and its face omitting $j$ is the original boundary face by the paired-deletion identification of Step 2. Thus it extends $a$ as a simplicial map. The criterion applied in Step 1 proves that $f$ is initial, equivalently that every $\operatorname{Map}_{P_x}(f,g)$ is weakly contractible.

source.place: Proposition 8.1.2.1, conclusion of the finite compatible extension argument.

proof.text: For the last clause take $f$ to be the degenerate identity at $x$. Its inverse is itself, and the two inverse triangles are constant two-simplices. Thus it is an equivalence by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], so the result already proved applies.

I checked them against Kerodon 03JW (Prop. 8.1.2.1, read online): the basic sets, pr(S) as a maximum, prioritized, and the ordering by priority then cardinality all match, as do the four horn cases. Those cases are: inner horn; k=d impossible; k=0 with i<n (identity edge); k=0 with i=n (edge f), the last two by Thm 4.4.2.6. Step 4 is correct: d>=n+1>=2 and k<d hold, and for i<n maximality of i forces i+1 into S, so the first edge is the identity at x. lean.statement: theorem twistedSourceFiber_equivalence_initial {C : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory C] (x : C _⦋0⦌) [Quasicategory (twistedSourceFiber C x)] : (∀ f : (twistedSourceFiber C x) _⦋0⦌, IsEquivalenceEdge C ((twistedSourceFiberInclusion C x).app _ f) → IsInitial (twistedSourceFiber C x) f) ∧ (∃ e : (twistedSourceFiber C x) _⦋0⦌, (twistedSourceFiberInclusion C x).app _ e = C.σ 0 x ∧ IsInitial (twistedSourceFiber C x) e)
